skill.name: recipe-manager
skill.description: Guides creation, conversion, validation, and maintenance of CookMode V2 recipe entries in recipes.js.
skill.summary: Manage structured CookMode V2 recipe data with consistent fields, components, notes, and validation checks.
skill.author: AdamFehse

security_audit.summary: The static command-execution findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline code formatting, and JavaScript template literals in SKILL.md. I found no prompt-injection language or malicious command intent. A low-severity issue remains because the skill documents an author-specific absolute local path.

remediation.issue: Hard-coded local filesystem path in documentation
remediation.suggestion: Replace the absolute user-specific path with a repo-relative path such as recipes.js, and instruct users to confirm the target file before edits.

content.value_statement: Recipe data can become inconsistent when ingredients, notes, and categories use different formats. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured recipe creation, conversion, and validation for recipes.js.
actual_capabilities: Defines the required recipe object fields for recipes.js entries.
Documents structured ingredient objects with amount, unit, ingredient, and optional prep fields.
Explains how to convert ingredient strings into structured objects.
Provides validation checks for slugs, categories, components, instructions, notes, images, and JavaScript syntax.
Shows examples for scaling, display formatting, notes, and a complete cookie recipe.
Identifies display category order and related CookMode V2 components.
limitations: Does not include executable scripts or automated validation tooling.
Assumes the CookMode V2 recipes.js schema and four fixed categories.
Does not verify live image URLs or external recipe sources on its own.
Includes a hard-coded local file path that users may need to replace.

use_cases.title: Add a New Recipe
use_cases.description: Create a recipe entry with a kebab-case slug, category, grouped ingredients, instructions, notes, and optional images.
use_cases.target_user: Home cook maintaining a personal recipe app

use_cases.title: Convert Ingredient Lists
use_cases.description: Turn free-form ingredient lines into structured amount, unit, ingredient, and prep fields for consistent scaling and display.

use_cases.title: Validate Recipe Content
use_cases.description: Review recipes for required fields, allowed categories, component arrays, note format, image URL presence, and JavaScript syntax concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Recipe
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a CookMode V2 recipe for [recipe name]. Use the recipes.js structure with category, components, ingredient fields, instructions, notes, and optional images.

prompt_templates.title: Convert Ingredient Text
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert these ingredient lines into structured recipe ingredient fields. Separate amount, unit, ingredient, and prep where possible: [paste ingredients].

prompt_templates.title: Audit Recipe Consistency
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this recipe entry for CookMode V2 compatibility. Check slug format, category, components, ingredient fields, instructions, notes, images, and JavaScript syntax.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Bulk Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a migration plan for converting these recipes into the CookMode V2 object format. Identify component groups, ambiguous quantities, missing fields, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: A user provides a cookie recipe with plain ingredient lines and preparation notes.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a structured recipe plan with category, components, normalized ingredients, baking steps, and texture notes.

output_examples.input: A user asks whether an existing recipe entry is valid for CookMode V2.
output: One ingredient is missing a unit.
Notes use an accepted text format.
Image URLs should be checked before publishing.

output_examples.input: A user wants to convert old ingredient strings into the object format.
output_examples.output: The skill separates quantities, units, ingredient names, and preparation notes, then flags any ambiguous items for human review.

best_practices: Confirm the target recipes.js file before making edits.
Keep ingredient names simple and place preparation details in the prep field.
Validate each recipe against the checklist before publishing changes.
anti_patterns: Do not mix plain ingredient strings with structured ingredient objects.
Do not add new categories unless the application display order is updated.
Do not assume external recipe text has complete quantities or units.

faq.question: What recipe format does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports the CookMode V2 recipes.js object format with categories, components, structured ingredients, instructions, notes, and optional images.

faq.question: Can it convert old ingredient strings?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains how to split ingredient text into amount, unit, ingredient, and optional prep fields.

faq.question: Does it run validation automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides a validation checklist and guidance, but it does not include an executable validator.

faq.question: Which categories are supported?
faq.answer: The documented categories are Entree, Side, Soup, and Dessert.

faq.question: Can it handle recipe notes?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents single text notes and multiple note entries as accepted formats.

faq.question: Is the documented file path portable?
faq.answer: No. The skill includes an author-specific local path, so users should replace it with their own project path.
